assumptions: Anchor is 'center' because the boxes are viewed from above and their centre is the metric position; 'bottom_center' is only the downstream AABB edge, not a wheel or ground-contact point.
Each tracked vehicle is treated as representing its driver and is assessed independently.
The mapped stop_zone and stop_line are assumed to belong to the approach to the stop-sign intersection in the rule; no separate stop-sign detection is available.
Inbound travel is the crossing from y<0.6 towards y>0.6, which the line description defines as direction 'to_right'.
Stopping is operationalised as remaining still in stop_zone for at least 1000 ms at a speed no greater than 0.05, using the DSL threshold for stopped/still, before the first crossing of stop_line.
A stop anywhere within stop_zone is treated as stopping at the near side of the intersection at the marked stop line.
No maximum interval is imposed between the stop and the subsequent crossing because the statute specifies none.
A vehicle that never crosses stop_line passes under the prescribed IMPLIES idiom.
The exception for directions from a police officer or traffic control signal is omitted because such directions are not encoded in the rule; the compiled rule covers the ordinary case.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: A vehicle may cross the stop line only if it has dwelled (stopped) in the stop zone before that first crossing.

provenance.reason: Tracked object is a vehicle; the driver is represented by the vehicle for evaluation.

The statute does not specify a measured point. Per line/zone notes, boxes are top-down and centre is the metric position, while bottom_center is the downstream AABB edge, not wheels; therefore centre is the evaluated anchor.

provenance.quote: shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line
at a clearly marked stop line

provenance.reason: The statute does not state a direction; direction is taken from the line description (approach from y<0.6 cross towards y>0.6, moving downwards (+y) = to_right).
The statute says the driver shall stop but gives no duration; 1000 ms is assumed as a minimum dwell to count as stopped in this encoding.
The statute says the driver shall stop but gives no numeric speed; 0.05 is the DSL threshold for stopped/still used to encode stopping.

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
